subject.title: fix(discord): preserve content-type and skip optimization for animated/WebP images

question: Should this Discord media fix expose `preserveWebp` and `preserveAvif` as public Plugin SDK options and make over-cap preserved media fail instead of recompressing, or should the repair stay Discord-owned on current main's media policy?
rationale: The unresolved blockers are public SDK contract scope and user-visible delivery semantics, so automation should not choose the permanent API or compatibility behavior without maintainer intent.

options.title: Refresh and narrow the contract
options.body: Rebase or replace the branch on current main, keep Discord-specific preservation out of the public SDK unless explicitly approved, preserve delivery compatibility where possible, and require live Discord proof before merge.

options.title: Approve the new media contract
options.body: Maintainers can intentionally accept public preserve options and fail-closed oversized preserved media, but the PR should document and prove that behavior before merge.

options.title: Replace the stale branch
options.body: If conflict repair is too costly, keep the linked issue open and use a fresh narrow fix that preserves contributor credit.

recommendation.title: Refresh and narrow the contract
recommendation.body: Rebase or replace the branch on current main, keep Discord-specific preservation out of the public SDK unless explicitly approved, preserve delivery compatibility where possible, and require live Discord proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the clearest sampled history on the Discord media send path and adjacent shared media helpers involved in the API and compatibility choice.
